analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (head line 3) and rewrites the Qwen27 TP assistant paragraph (base/head line 2456). The new text says plain `darkbloom cluster` plans without the embedded assistant under default `auto`, because a coordinator-registered setup carries none and the assistant is not qualified for public traffic. Explicit `on` keeps the assistant, and the pair is then not offered to the coordinator. `darkbloom cluster local` serves the assistant locally.

No code, controls or endpoints change, so I found no regression against TB-002, TB-007, TB-011 or T-041. The rewrite narrows what the docs say about the public-traffic exposure of the unqualified assistant. This is documentation only: I could not verify here that the code actually enforces the described gating (not offering the pair to the coordinator under explicit `on`, and omitting the assistant in coordinator-registered setups). That enforcement lives in provider-swift cluster placement code, outside the supplied evidence.

Base units 7 and 8 and head unit 9 contain no other changed lines. Their context (cache settings, LaunchAgent env passthrough, prefix-cache defaults, App Attest worker flag) is unchanged and out of scope. Head unit 9 ends at line 385, so the changed paragraph at head line 2456 is not visible in it; I relied on the patch excerpt and the base text for that paragraph. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I cannot rule out other hunks, but the range map is marked complete and lists only lines 3 and 2456.
